o1.biggest_strength: Ranks channels by users who actually stayed with the arithmetic shown, and turns the 58% migration-ticket history into eight hard gates timed to the 1 December freeze.
o1.biggest_mistake: The single biggest risk in the data — 3 support staff, 31-hour replies, 2,400 tickets — gets only an unquantified 'under 8 hours' target with no rota or coverage plan, and the drafts are littered with [bracketed] blanks.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Staff launch-week support concretely (who covers which hours, which wave-hold thresholds trigger) and fill every placeholder so the X posts and email could be pasted and sent.

o2.biggest_strength: Splits the launch so new users still go on 8 December even if the migration gate fails (they have no settings to lose), moves Product Hunt and Hacker News to 15 December, and puts an owner and a ticket-rate threshold on every step.
o2.biggest_mistake: The launch email credits 'the community' but names no extension author, breaking the always-credit rule, and a 95% tester pass gate is softer than the developer persona's 'please don't break my hotkeys'.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Name three extension authors and their extensions in the launch email and tighten the migration gate to zero reported hotkey or setting losses before the 1 December freeze.

reason: Output 2 is the one I'd hand to the team tomorrow: every date has an owner, the rollout waves have real thresholds and a plan B, and it sensibly lets new users launch even if migration slips. Output 1 has the better X thread and stricter 'zero lost hotkeys' gate, but its answer to the support flood is a target with no staffing behind it.
